blocks.text: South Slope: streets and boundaries

items.t: South Slope is the house pocket on the hill between Rumble Street at the top and Marine Drive at the bottom: the City's Royal Oak Community Plan map draws this slope with Rumble Street, Royal Oak Avenue, Marine Drive and Gilley Avenue as its working street frame.

The plan map names the slope's creeks, which double as its internal boundaries: Frogger's Creek, Gray Creek, John Matthews Creek and Byrne Creek all cross the plan area between Rumble Street and Marine Drive.

blocks.text: South Slope: the housing stock

items.t: The slope's existing form is low: the Royal Oak Community Plan's existing-height map shows the residential blocks south of Rumble Street at one to three storeys, with four storeys appearing only toward the station area.

blocks.text: South Slope: rules that affect buyers

items.t: The Royal Oak Community Plan, adopted in March 2025, is the plan layer for the slope's northern half: its Station Area District is bounded by Nelson Avenue to the west, MacPherson Avenue to the east, Imperial Street to the north and Rumble Street to the south.

blocks.text: South Slope: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: Two of the slope's schools are on Rumble Street's edge, not inside the house blocks: Clinton Elementary, kindergarten to Grade 7, at 5858 Clinton Street, and Burnaby South Secondary at 5455 Rumble Street both appear on the Royal Oak plan map as slope anchors.
Nelson Elementary is the slope's west-side school, at 4850 Irmin Street, and the Royal Oak plan map places Nelson Park beside it, above Rumble Street.
The bus that loops the slope also defines its edges: route 148 stops run along Rumble Street, down Nelson Avenue, along Marine Drive, and back up Gilley Avenue, tracing the pocket's perimeter.

blocks.text: South Slope: development and new projects

items.t: Royal Oak Community Plan, the slope's northern half and the Royal Oak Station area, City of Burnaby, community plan: covers the Station Area District between Nelson Avenue, MacPherson Avenue, Imperial Street and Rumble Street, and the slope streets down to Marine Drive — status: adopted March 2025 (as of November 3, 2026).

blocks.text: South Slope: costs and taxes

items.t: The slope-relevant utility line is garbage: the City's 2026 residential garbage disposal fee runs from $73 a year for a 120-litre toter to $447 for a 360-litre toter, with the 180-litre default at $159, before the 5% early-payment discount.

blocks.text: South Slope: getting around

items.t: Route 148 is the slope's own bus: TransLink runs it from Royal Oak Station via Beresford Street, Royal Oak Avenue, Rumble Street, Nelson Avenue, Marine Drive and Gilley Avenue to Edmonds Station, linking both ends of the pocket to the Expo Line.

Marine Drive is the bottom-edge road: it runs along the foot of the slope toward Vancouver at Boundary Road and toward New Westminster in the other direction, and the 148's Marine Drive stops serve the lowest South Slope streets.

blocks.text: South Slope: risks and due diligence

items.t: Check the SPEA boundary on every creek-adjacent lot: the City's application checklist requires site plans to identify applicable Streamside Protection and Enhancement Areas and any geotechnical hazards or setbacks, and on this slope the creek, not the property line, often sets the buildable area.

Check slope and drainage together: the Royal Oak plan maps open watercourses across the slope between Rumble Street and Marine Drive, so a lot can be affected by both a ravine bank and uphill runoff; the plan map shows the watercourses, not a lot-level geotechnical conclusion.

blocks.text: South Slope home prices: what sold, November 2025 to October 2026

47 condos sold in South Slope with a median price of $621,000 (the middle half sold between $551,750 and $698,750), taking a median of 29 days to sell at 97.2% of the last list price; 9% sold above list. They had a median $672 per square foot, a median year built of 1996 and a median strata fee of $471 a month. 37 houses sold in South Slope with a median price of $1,860,000 (the middle half sold between $1,700,000 and $2,325,000), taking a median of 30 days to sell at 94.8% of the last list price; 5% sold above list. They had a median $610 per square foot, a median year built of 1979 and a median lot of 7,315 square feet.

faq.q: How many homes are for sale in South Slope?
faq.a: At the end of October 2026 the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® figures showed 33 houses and 38 condos and townhomes listed in South Slope. Those are month-end counts and they move daily, so ask Jared for a current list.

faq.q: Is South Slope a buyers’ or sellers’ market?
faq.a: In October 2026, houses had a sales ratio of 12% (a balanced market); condos and townhomes had 18% (a balanced market). The sales ratio is homes sold divided by homes listed; on the reports’ scale under 12% favours buyers, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% favours sellers. One month in one community is a small sample, so look at the monthly table above before you decide.

faq.q: How many homes sold in South Slope from June to October 2026?
faq.a: 22 houses and 33 condos and townhomes sold in South Slope over those 5 months; detached houses peaked in June with 5 sold and condos and townhomes peaked in September with 10 sold.

faq.q: How big is South Slope compared with the rest of Burnaby?
faq.a: In October 2026, South Slope held 7.7% of the 430 detached houses listed in Burnaby and 2.9% of the 1,309 condos and townhomes listed in Burnaby.

faq.q: What mix of houses and condos is for sale in South Slope?
faq.a: In October 2026, houses made up 46.5% of the 71 homes listed in South Slope and condos and townhomes made up 53.5%; of the 11 that sold, houses were 36.4% and condos and townhomes 63.6%.

faq.q: Are there more or fewer homes for sale in South Slope than in June?
faq.a: Listings of detached houses fell from 43 in June to 33 in October 2026 (−23.3%); condos and townhomes fell from 49 in June to 38 in October 2026 (−22.4%).

faq.q: Which elementary school is actually on the slope?
faq.a: Heritage Burnaby records that the combined school opened in 1992 and replaced the former Jericho Hill School for the Deaf in Vancouver. 41 (Burnaby) before relying on it.

faq.q: Where do students go after South Slope Elementary?
faq.a: The secondary anchor for this side of Burnaby is Burnaby South Secondary, Grades 8 to 12, at 5455 Rumble Street, at the top of the slope. Address alone does not assign a student; confirm with the district.

faq.q: Does the creek behind a house limit what I can build?
faq.a: It can, and on this slope that is a common question because Frogger's Creek, Gray Creek, John Matthews Creek and Byrne Creek all cross the pocket. Burnaby's streams guide states that development within 30 metres of a stream triggers the streamside rules, with leave areas of 15 to 30 metres for Class A fish-bearing watercourses, set for the specific site by the Planning Department.

faq.q: Is there salmon in the creek at the bottom of the slope?
faq.a: Yes, in Byrne Creek. The Byrne Creek Streamkeepers, listed by the Burnaby Lake Park Association among Burnaby's streamkeeper groups, describe Byrne Creek draining a large urban watershed along the south slope of Burnaby, running through a ravine park and spawning habitat into the Fraser River, with rejuvenated populations of coho salmon, chum salmon and cutthroat trout monitored by volunteers.

faq.q: What did condos in South Slope sell for?
faq.a: 47 condos sold in South Slope between November 1, 2025 to October 22, 2026, with a median price of $621,000.

faq.q: How long do condos take to sell in South Slope?
faq.a: The median was 29 days from listing to sale, and homes sold at a median 97.2% of the last list price (9% sold above list), for sales November 1, 2025 to October 22, 2026.
